# The Name Atlantís and the World It Opens

A name is a door. Atlantís opens onto lost island, legendary realm, sea. Atlantís (atlantis) — 'daughter of Atlas' — is the island empire Plato sets beyond the Pillars of Heracles in the Timaeus and Critias: a naval power defeated by a prehistoric Athens and swallowed by the sea in a single day and night. Atlantís is the legendary island civilization described by Plato, a powerful naval empire that angered the gods and sank beneath the waves. The tale functions in the dialogues as a philosophical counter-image to ideal Athens — the archetype of the golden age destroyed by its own ambition — and antiquity already debated whether it was history or parable. PÚNYCODEX restores the name as Atlantís and serves its temple at atlantís.com. The original preserves one prosodic feature — the acute accent on the final iota — rather...

## Domain and Meaning

The temple domain is **Lost Island, Legendary Realm, Sea**. The traditional meaning is "Daughter of Atlas; the legendary lost island civilization." Together, those two facts explain why the name mattered enough to be remembered for millennia.

## The Mythic Landscape

Atlantís is Plato's story , whether invented or adapted from older traditions. It serves as a philosophical allegory about the corruption of power and the fragility of civilization. Myth is the memory of a civilization, and names are the hooks on which that memory hangs.

## Modern Patterns

The [Patterns](/sites/atlantis/patterns/) page maps the industries and sister temples that share Atlantís's current. A name that once organized ritual now organizes search, advertising, and creative collaboration.

## Join the Restoration

You can support the work through the [Patron](/sites/atlantis/patron/) wall, submit creative work, or simply share the address. Every visit to Atlantís is a vote for original scripts.

## Why This Restoration Matters

Restoring Atlantís is part of a larger effort to make the web multilingual by default. The PÚNYCODEX project does not ask users to learn a new alphabet; it asks the infrastructure to respect the alphabets that already exist. A single Unicode domain is a small proof, but it is a proof that scales: every name restored makes the next one easier.

## The PÚNYCODEX Angle

The PÚNYCODEX project treats Atlantís as more than a curiosity. It is a proof that the domain-name system can carry the full weight of human naming, from Greek to the modern browser. Every visit to this temple is a small act of preservation.

## For Developers and Linguists

The PÚNYCODEX dataset exposes Atlantís through a versioned API, making the restoration usable by search engines, localization pipelines, and scholarly tools. Because the canonical sources are stored as structured JSON, every improvement flows automatically to the temple, the extension, and the mobile app.

## Visit the Temple

If this post sparked your curiosity, the [home page](/sites/atlantis/) offers the full name breakdown, the [lore page](/sites/atlantis/lore/) explores the myth, and the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/atlantis/scholars/) provides the footnotes. Each page is a doorway into the same restoration.

## Why This Name Still Travels

Names like Atlantís do not retire. They resurface in translations, in adaptations, in brand names, and in scholarly debates because they still do useful cultural work. Keeping the original spelling alive in a domain is one way to make sure that work continues in the digital layer.

## A Note on the Address Bar

When you type Atlantís, the browser performs an invisible conversion into Punycode so the global DNS can route the request. The user sees the original name; the machines see a compatible ASCII encoding. That duality is the engineering compromise that makes the restoration possible, and it is the reason every Unicode domain is both a technical milestone and a small act of cultural memory.
